description: Drafted the Steve Hall automotive pricing proposal full of em-dashes (headings, body copy, table cells) and referenced the source coffee meeting/conversation directly ('as discussed', 'the conversation', 'following coffee discussion') plus an unrelated past engagement (a prior personal/business AI implementation project) and a pharmaceutical-client precedent. identity/writing-rules.md bans em-dashes outright in all content written on David's behalf, format-agnostic, and David separately asked that the document stay scoped to this project only with no meeting references. Neither rule was checked before the draft was produced.
correction: Before finalizing any generated document, scan for em-dash characters (regex —|–) and remove them per writing-rules.md. For client-facing scoping documents, keep content scoped strictly to the project at hand; do not reference the internal discovery conversation as a source or pull in unrelated past engagements/precedents unless explicitly asked.
systemic_fix: Run an em-dash scan as a standing pre-finalize check on all generated client documents (not just emails), and default to project-scoped content in proposal drafts, holding meeting attribution and unrelated precedents out unless the user asks for them.
